title: How a Toaster Knows
summary: How a pop-up toaster holds the bread down, heats it with glowing wires, and lets a bending metal strip decide when to pop it up.

pages.section: Hook: nobody watches the toast, yet it stops on time
pages.say: You drop the bread in and walk away, and somehow it pops up done. Nobody is watching it, so how does the toaster know when to stop? The answer is inside the slot.

beats.object: a tomato-red pop-up toaster on a wooden counter
beats.action: inks itself in, outline first, then its colour floods in
drop from above into the two slots

beats.object: the side lever and the browning dial
beats.action: their cream tags ink in along leader lines
a dark gap between the slices shows the wires waiting below

pages.section: Pushing the lever down locks the bread in and turns the power on
pages.say: Pushing the lever lowers a little tray, the carriage, with the bread on it. At the bottom a hook catches it and holds it there against a spring. The same push closes a switch, so current starts to flow.

beats.action: sinks and lights mustard as the lever slides down its groove

beats.object: the carriage tray seen through a cut-away side window
beats.action: slides down carrying both slices
snaps over the carriage tab and holds it

beats.object: a coiled spring under the carriage
beats.action: stretches tight and stays stretched

beats.object: a pair of switch contacts at the base
beats.action: press together and the green lamp turns on

pages.section: The heat comes from wires that resist the current
pages.say: Current runs through thin nichrome wire wound on flat sheets beside each slice. Nichrome resists the current, so it heats up until it glows red. That glow is radiant heat, and it browns the bread's surface.

beats.object: flat sheets wound with thin wire, seen through the side window
beats.action: ink in on both sides of each slice
darken, then shift to orange-red, coil by coil

beats.object: the 'heat' step pill and the wires
beats.action: the pill lights mustard while the wires glow full red

beats.object: the bread surface facing the wires
beats.action: turns from cream to golden brown, edges first

pages.section: A strip of two metals bends as it warms and acts as the clock
pages.say: Next to the wires sits a bimetal strip: two metals bonded together. When it warms, one metal stretches more than the other, so the strip slowly curls. The browning dial sets how far it must curl before anything happens.

beats.object: a bimetal strip beside the latch, close up
beats.action: inks in, its two layers drawn in two colours
one layer lengthens past the other
bends slowly toward the latch as heat rises
beats.camera: push in on the strip tip

beats.action: turns, moving the strip's target farther away

pages.section: The strip trips the latch, the spring pops the toast, the power cuts
pages.say: When the strip curls far enough, it nudges the hook off the carriage. The stretched spring yanks the tray up, the switch opens, and the wires go dark. Your toast pops up, done by a strip of metal that felt the heat.

beats.action: touches the latch hook and pushes it aside
spring snaps short, carriage shoots up

beats.object: the wire coils and the lamp
beats.action: fade from red to grey; the lamp goes out
pop up out of the slots and settle half out
lights mustard as the last step, toast standing ready
